en: The Sadhana of Tārā for Deceiving Death.
Having meditated upon her as before, up to the limit of emptiness,
one should visualize her seated upon a moon-disc in the center of a white lotus,
bound in the vajra-paryaṅka posture, and holding a boon-granting gesture and an utpala lotus.
Having the form of the autumn moonbeams, seated upon a moon at her back, fully adorned with all ornaments, and possessing the physical appearance of a sixteen-year-old; Mvts_2 //
Having meditated on Noble Tārā in his heart, one should visualize her wheel, white in luster,
consisting of eight compartments and filled with eight syllables.

With a one-pointed mind and firm resolve, one should meditate for six months upon the navel [of the deity], wherein the name of the person to be accomplished (sādhya) is placed in the middle of the syllable *oṃ* and the letter *ha*. Mvts 4.
One should recite this ten-syllable mantra with an undaunted mind.
In this regard, the mantra is: Oṃ tāre tuttāre ture svāhā.
One who meditates on the wheel of Tārā’s heart will not be stained by the defects of death;
devoted to this practice, they shall attain all siddhis within the limit of six months.
The Sādhana of Tārā for Deceiving Death.
